No snippet contradicts the fact. The corpus provides strong, repeated corroboration with no conflict.

scores.rationale: Multiple snippets directly support the use of Weibull and Gompertz models to describe ageing-related survivorship/mortality patterns: [1] ranked Gompertz first for actuarial senescence in birds, [3] found senescence generally described by the Gompertz model across taxa, [4] and [13] fit Weibull functions to plant survival data to separate baseline and senescent mortality, [8] and [14] discuss Gompertz law describing mortality, and [10] explicitly uses Gompertz parameters for ageing. These give moderate-to-strong corroboration. Some snippets contradict universality: [2] shows Weibull can be inaccurate when mortality concentrates in specific life stages, and [18] documents age-independent (constant) mortality in a long-lived herb, indicating exceptions. However, the stylized fact says 'typically well described,' which these exceptions do not overturn. Overall the corpus corroborates the fact (consensus_direction 3) with moderate evidence strength (2), since several relevant references affirm Weibull/Gompertz applicability while a couple note limitations.

Only snippet 14 offers a caveat—Weibull can be inaccurate when mortality is concentrated in specific life stages—but this qualifies rather than overturns the general fact. Overall the evidence is strong and consistent, supporting the stylized fact.
